reason: A Hebrew man explicitly questions Moses' authority, asking 'Who made you a ruler and judge over us?' (מִי שָֽׂמְךָ לְאִ֨ישׁ שַׂ֤ר וְשֹׁפֵט֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ - Exodus 2:14). This represents Hebrew people voicing direct criticism against an assumed leader. The criticism challenges Moses' right to judicial authority over the Hebrew people. While the passage does not include criticism directed at Yahweh (only the 'leaders' component of the statement applies), the presence of Hebrew criticism against a leadership figure satisfies the condition posed by the statement.
